morning.caption:
Washington has been nudging two of OPEC's founders toward the door. Reuters, citing 10 people, reports the US encouraged Venezuela and Iraq this year to consider leaving the group and blocked Venezuela's dues.

The State Department says top officials never raised it. Iraq stayed and is pushing for a bigger quota.

Watch Sunday, Nov. 29, when OPEC+ sets 2027 policy.

midday.caption:
840,000 barrels a day. That is what Trans Mountain shipped on average in the third quarter, up from 777,000 a year ago, and the line can now carry up to about 980,000 after an additive project finished two months early.

Revenue was C$825 million and C$551 million went back to Ottawa.

evening.caption:
A second Saudi refinery has been targeted in two days. A projectile struck Aramco's Jazan plant on the Red Sea coast on Thursday, killing a worker and halting some units, a day after the Houthis claimed attacks on Ras Tanura.

Jazan sits on the side of the kingdom Saudi exports would lean on if Gulf terminals were shut.

Who feels it: shippers and buyers already planning around Hormuz.
